text:
sam.k: Quick Q — follow-up for the multi-region RFC: when a tenant is EU-resident and the primary region goes down, what's our expected behavior if we route write traffic to a US standby? do we: 1) fail closed (403), 2) soft-forward after consent check, or 3) retry with escrow/async-handback? Need a short decision + who owns implementation.

anne: Short answer: we shouldn't silently violate residency. Options depend on the consent matrix and SLA tier. We outlined two safe defaults in the RFC but didn't pick one.

pj: Runtime note: the serving runtime currently has a "lease+escrow" mode that can accept writes into an escrow queue tagged with origin-region. Escrow requires a later handback to original region for finality.

misha: Technical constraints: escrow helps availability but complicates KV cache coherency and embeddings replication. If we accept in US, reads may surface non-final data unless we bubble TTLs and consistency flags.

legal-bot: Policy: any PII/data covered by EU residency must not be stored or processed in a non-EU region unless explicit customer consent is recorded and auditable. Consent must be tied to a timestamped token.

infra-oncall: Operationally, we need a clear playbook: metrics for "consent_check_latency", "escrow_queue_depth", and a circuit-breaker to stop forwarding when escrow depth or consent failure rate crosses threshold.

lucy: UX/API idea: client can set header X-Residence-Action: allow-fallback | fail-closed | async-escrow. Default = fail-closed. Also expose explanation in error payload so integrators can decide.

ranjit: Implementation sketch:
```
POST /v1/deployments/{id}/inference
Headers: X-Residence-Action: allow-fallback
Body: { tenant_id: "t-123", residency: "EU" }
```
Server flow:
1) check residency flag; 2) if primary down -> consult consent service; 3) if consent ok -> forward to standby and mark write with escrow_token; 4) if no consent -> return 403 with code RESIDENCY_BLOCKED.

sam.k: Question: if we do escrow, how do we guarantee idempotency and prevent double-apply when the original region comes back? also what about billing — do we charge per-token on standby + reconciliation?

pj: For idempotency: require client-supplied idempotency_key (or server-generated request_id). Escrow records include request_id; reconciliation attempts to dedupe. Billing: we should bill for execution in standby; reconciliation is metadata-only. Put this in billing doc.

misha: Cache implications: tag cached responses with "finality": pending|final. Clients should be able to request only-final reads or accept pending with a warning header X-Redwood-Finality.

anne: Proposal for decision (pick one):
A) Fail-closed by default; allow-fallback only with explicit consent header and tenant-level opt-in. Simpler, legally safe, slower migrations.
B) Soft-forward (escrow) for SLA tier "enterprise" with consent audit trail; default still fail-closed.
C) Async-escrow for non-PII tenants: accelerate availability but mark responses as pending.
Please react with +1 to prefer or comment other.

lucy: +1 to A as default (we should be conservative). :+1:
ranjit: +1 to B for enterprise customers who paid for cross-region availability.

pj: +1 to hybrid: default=A, enterprise=B, non-sensitive=C. Will draft service flags.

misha: Noted: will add cache header semantics and a reconciliation task to eng-ml backlog.

anne: Action items:
- pj: write runtime flag and config (policy = residency.fail_behavior) + tests (owner)
- ranjit: open API PR for X-Residence-Action header + error codes (owner)
- misha: add cache/finality headers and integration tests with KV cache (owner)
- infra-oncall: add playbook metrics and runbook items for escrow overload (owner)
- legal-bot: provide consent token schema and retention notes (owner)

sam.k: Thanks — can we decide on deadlines? I propose RFC follow-up patch by EOW and a small tech spike next week to validate latency hit for consent checks.

pj: EOW for config + spike next week works for me.

anne: I'll capture this decision in the RFC follow-up doc and tag @product for prioritization.

infra-oncall: tagging runbook checklist here: https://go/runbooks/region-handoff (ops link)

ranjit: FYI I'll include an example error response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error":"RESIDENCY_BLOCKED",
  "reason":"Tenant policy: EU-only. Request routed to US while no consent.",
  "help":"Set X-Residence-Action or contact account team"
}
```

sam.k: cool. closing thread once RFC follow-up PR is up. thanks all. :raised_hands:
